audits.decision_reason: All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies a concrete causal path from inter-subject autonomic reactivity differences (measured by SRI from cvxEDA phasic driver and HRV reactivity) to Mondrian conformal undercoverage via violation of within-subject exchangeability between calibration and test windows. Variables are measurable from WESAD E4 data, confounders are identified, and the prediction is testable via correlation and downsampling controls.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism links subject-specific movement artifact profiles (MAI from ACC) to PPG/EDA signal corruption, feature distribution shift between calibration and test phases, and inflated conformity score variance causing quantile overestimation. Domain-specific boundary conditions (Empatica E4 wrist placement, WESAD TSST seated protocol, ACC range) are specified. The prediction is testable via partial correlation controlling for general signal quality (SQI) and MMD analysis.

The causal chain contains a logical gap: it asserts that contamination of baseline-class calibration samples narrows stress-class prediction intervals because 'Mondrian uses per-class quantiles', but per-class quantile estimation for the stress class uses only stress-labeled calibration samples. Baseline contamination would affect the baseline quantile, not the stress quantile, unless the nonconformity score function pools information across classes (e.g., 1 - softmax(true class)), which is not specified in the mechanism.
audits.salvage_note: Repair by specifying the nonconformity function (e.g., 1 - predicted probability of true class from a multi-class classifier) and demonstrating how baseline contamination biases the classifier's stress-class probability estimates, thereby shifting stress conformity scores. Alternatively, redefine the mechanism to involve contamination of the stress stratum itself if post-TSST windows are mislabeled as stress.

audits.decision_reason: All critical checks pass. The mechanism proposes that low interoceptive awareness (proxied by label-physiology discrepancy) causes self-report mislabeling in calibration, leading to Mondrian computing conformity scores against incorrect class-conditional distributions. Variables are measurable (PSI from physiological features, self-report from questionnaires, discrepancy as proxy). The simulated mislabeling experiment provides a concrete test. Confounders like alexithymia and social desirability are identified.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism identifies a specific failure of Mondrian's discrete protocol-based stratification: continuous within-condition stress intensity (WSI) varies across subjects due to trait anxiety, causing feature distribution shifts that make calibration conformity scores non-representative for high-WSI subjects. The re-stratification experiment (WSI tertile vs. random variable) provides a strong distinguishing test against the arbitrary-stratification rival.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism links uncontrolled recording time (09:00-17:00) to circadian variation in baseline autonomic tone, causing baseline feature distributions to shift toward stress distributions for evening subjects and violating stratum-wise exchangeability. The simultaneous regression of coverage on recording time and session duration cleanly distinguishes circadian effects from fatigue. Domain-specific boundary conditions (cortisol rhythm, Empatica E4, Mondrian baseline stratum) are well-specified.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism posits that subject-heterogeneous high-order feature interactions (EDA×HRV×respiration) create conformity score distributions that marginal label-only stratification cannot capture. The interaction weight (logistic regression coefficient) and KL divergence between calibration/test conformity scores are measurable. The comparison of interaction-aware stratification against PCA dimensionality reduction provides a specific test against the curse-of-dimensionality rival.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism addresses finite-sample behavior of Mondrian conformal prediction: rare physiological phenotypes (identified via GMM clustering on subject-level stress response features) have small effective calibration sizes, leading to high-variance and downward-biased empirical quantiles. The matching design (subsampling common-phenotype calibration windows to match rare-phenotype effective size) isolates phenotype rarity from calibration size effects.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies a concrete thermoregulatory pathway: stress-induced cutaneous blood flow changes alter wrist skin temperature (measured by E4 thermistor), which shifts EDA baseline and gain via temperature-dependent sweat gland conductance (5-10%/°C), causing calibration-test feature distribution shifts. The temperature correction (k=0.07/°C) vs. session-time detrending comparison cleanly tests against the sensor-aging rival.

The causal chain is incomplete: it questions whether 'Mondrian uses all classes for normalization' but does not specify the nonconformity function. Under standard Mondrian with per-class quantiles, baseline contamination affects only the baseline quantile. The mechanism must explain how contaminated baseline conformity scores narrow the stress-class prediction interval (e.g., via a shared classifier whose stress-class probability estimates are biased by baseline contamination).
audits.salvage_note: Repair by specifying the nonconformity function (e.g., 1 - softmax probability of true class from a multi-class Random Forest) and showing how baseline windows with stress-like physiology receive high stress-class probability, biasing the classifier's calibration and shifting stress conformity scores. Alternatively, define a conformity score that explicitly uses all class probabilities.
